story.text: In bugaku, the dance repertoire of Japanese court music, the dance Ama is followed by a piece called Ni-no-mai, 'the second dance'. In it two masked dancers, an old man with a laughing face and an old woman with a swollen one, try to copy the Ama dance and get it comically wrong. From this, performing the second dance came to mean imitating someone else and failing in the same way.

bad.s: 重[おも]い荷物[にもつ]を持[も]ち上[あ]げたら、{腰[こし]を据[す]えて}しまった。
bad.en: (meant: I lifted a heavy bag and hurt my back)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with injury. For hurting your back say koshi o itameru.

bad.s: 先生[せんせい]はいつも{腰[こし]を据[す]えて}いて、誰[だれ]にでも丁寧[ていねい]だ。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher is always humble and polite to everyone)
bad.why: Humble manners are koshi ga hikui; this idiom is about settling in for a long effort.

mean: to finally get round to acting
lit: to lift one's heavy hips: to heave oneself up at last

use.how: Verb phrase, usually with やっと／ついに／ようやく: 市がようやく重い腰を上げた. Said about a person or organisation acting after long delay.

near.diff: 腰が重い describes the habit of being slow to act; 重い腰を上げる is the moment one finally does act.

cue: Tenants complained about the leaking roof for months; the landlord finally sent someone to fix it. What did the landlord do?

ctx.s: 部屋[へや]が散[ち]らかりすぎて、ついに{重[おも]い腰[こし]を上[あ]げて}掃除[そうじ]を始[はじ]めた。
ctx.en: My room got so messy that I finally got round to cleaning it.

ctx.s: 何年[なんねん]も迷[まよ]っていた父[ちち]が、やっと{重[おも]い腰[こし]を上[あ]げて}健康[けんこう]診断[しんだん]を受[う]けた。
ctx.en: After putting it off for years, my father finally went for a health check.

ctx.s: 「確定申告[かくていしんこく]、もう済[す]んだ？」「締[し]め切[き]り直前[ちょくぜん]に{重[おも]い腰[こし]を上[あ]げた}ところ」
ctx.en: "Have you done your tax return?" "I've only just got round to it, right before the deadline."

ctx.s: 住民[じゅうみん]の苦情[くじょう]が相次[あいつ]ぎ、市[し]もようやく{重[おも]い腰[こし]を上[あ]げた}。
ctx.en: After a stream of complaints from residents, the city finally took action.

ctx.s: 批判[ひはん]を受[う]けて、会社[かいしゃ]はついに{重[おも]い腰[こし]を上[あ]げ}、調査[ちょうさ]を始[はじ]めた。
ctx.en: Under criticism, the company at last stirred itself and began an investigation.

ctx.s: 夫[おっと]が{重[おも]い腰[こし]を上[あ]げる}のを待[ま]っていたら、いつまでも庭[にわ]の手入[てい]れができない。
ctx.en: If I wait for my husband to get round to it, the garden will never get done.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]は毎朝[まいあさ]五時[ごじ]に{重[おも]い腰[こし]を上[あ]げて}、ジョギングしている。
bad.en: (meant: he gets up at five every morning and goes jogging)
bad.why: It marks one action finally taken after long delay, not a diligent daily habit.

bad.s: すぐに行動[こうどう]する彼[かれ]は、いつも{重[おも]い腰[こし]を上[あ]げる}のが早[はや]い。
bad.en: (meant: he acts at once and is always quick off the mark)
bad.why: The image presupposes reluctance. For someone quick to act say koshi ga karui or futtowaaku ga karui.
